extract.note: wikidata: written by a language model; the GPT-NL paper (https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.00920, section 4.2.1) says "An LLM, Phi-4 (Abdin et al., 2024, MIT-licensed;), was used to paraphrase these outputs". youtube-commons: machine-translated; section 4.2.2 says "The remaining transcripts were translated into Dutch via the open-source MADLAD-400 machine-translation model". cc_english-pd, cc_german-pd, cc_loc-pd-books, cc_eurovoc: taken from Common Corpus, whose paper (https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.01732, section 5) says "We developed OCRonos model based on Llama 3 8B ... It supports the correction of OCR errors" and "On highly deteriorated content, OCRonos can act as a synthetic rewriting tool", for its Open Culture and Open Government collections, without marking which records it corrected: a doubt; the collection metadata says of CC-English-PD and CC-German-PD: "Data is OCRd. Then, the poor OCR quality was solved through the development of OCR correction tools." european-parliament, naturalis, pbl, wikiwijs: every record's license reads "CC-BY", with no version (all rows, datasets-server statistics), and CC BY before 4.0 is refused, so no record of theirs could enter. dataset_stats.yaml and ALL_PARQUET_FILES_VALID in each folder are GPT-NL's file statistics and an empty marker file, not records.

Citation: Jesse J. Van Oort, Frank Brinkkemper, Erik de Graaf, Bram Vanroy and Saskia Lensink, "GPT-NL Public Corpus: A Permissively Licensed, Dutch-First Dataset for LLM Pre-training", Proceedings of LREC 2026, https://aclanthology.org/2026.lrec-1.548/. licenses.text:
Records whose license field reads exactly 'public-domain', 'Public domain', 'Public Domain'.

The dataset card says: "this is the license of the corpus. However, all datapoints have specific licenses attributed in the <license> metadata field. These licenses are based on the license of the original source dataset that was curated or augmented for the purpose of creating the GPT-NL public corpus." Its field table says: "license| license of the document (public domain/CC-0/CC-by)".

The publisher labels each of these records as being in the public domain, and that label is the record's proof (docs/licenses.md, "The publication decides" and "Per record", maintainer's decision, 2026-10-23). The collection metadata (https://huggingface.co/datasets/GPT-NL/Collection-metadata) describes the collections so labelled:

- American-stories: "The dataset has a CC-BY 4.0 license. The content itself is all in the public domain." "The dataset is drawn entirely from image scans in the public domain that are freely available for download from the Library of Congress's website."
- Koninklijke Bibliotheek (kb, kb-open-kranten, kb-pd-books): "those parts of these collections for which it can reasonably be assumed that the copyright has expired, i.e. digitised newspapers 1618-1885, digitised books 1780-1800, and digitised Public Domain books and periodicals fromt the DBNL collection."
- Utrechts Archief: "Utrechts Archief collections > 100 years old". The paper says of the archive collections: "All included works are at least 100 years old and often at least several decades older."
- Nationaal Archief: "Nationaal Archief administers the VOC archive."
- Woogle: "Public Decision documents that have to be made open by the Dutch Government".
- De Rechtspraak (rechtspraak): "Uitspraken" (court rulings) "scraped from rechtspraak.nl with permission from De Rechtspraak."
- Officiële Bekendmakingen, Openraadsinformatie, Tweede Kamer, Auditdienst Rijk, Noord-Hollands Archief, Zeeuws Archief: license "public-domain", published by Dutch government bodies and archives.
- CC-OpenAlex (cc_openalex): Common Corpus "filtered OpenAlex on CC-By, Public Domain/CC-0 and CC-BY-SA"; its "Public Domain" records enter.

No license text applies: a work in the public domain carries no rights.
